# `Q-12-14` — Listing `type: custom` Without `template:` Path

> A listing declares `type: custom` but no `template:` path;
> the `default` built-in is used instead.

## What this means

A listing of `type: custom` needs a `template:` value pointing
at the doctemplate that renders the items. With no `template:`,
there is nothing custom about the listing — Quarto falls back
to the `default` built-in template and emits this warning so
the author knows the configuration is incomplete.

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **A copy-paste mistake** where `type: custom` was kept but
  the matching `template:` line was not.
- **A migration in progress** — the author set `type: custom`
  intending to add the template path later.

## How to fix

Either supply a `template:` path:

```yaml
listing:
  type: custom
  template: my-template.template
```

or change `type:` to one of the built-in types (`default`,
`grid`, `table`) if you did not need a custom template after
all.

## Related

- `Q-12-7` — the reverse: `template:` set without
  `type: custom`.
- `Q-12-8` — `template:` set, but the file at that path could
  not be read.
